reviews.title: subscription fraud
reviews.text:
Honestly, this has been such a frustrating experience. I signed up for what I understood to be a free trial and canceled on the day it was supposed to end, yet I was still left with a $40 charge. I had to pay it out of my own pocket because the unpaid balance was preventing me from downloading and updating apps on my phone. This was money I worked hard to save as a reseller who isn’t able to get a job in this horrible market industry, and I never intended to spend it on a subscription I thought I had canceled in time.

I’ve tried contacting Apple support and PictureThis support (the app never responded) but i requested a refund through Apple, but I’ve gotten nowhere. It’s incredibly frustrating to spend money on something you didn’t intend to purchase and then struggle to get any help resolving the situation.

The app itself is one thing, but this entire billing and customer support experience has left a terrible impression on me. Customers shouldn’t have to go through this much stress trying to resolve an unexpected charge. I genuinely hope this gets addressed because this experience has completely changed how I feel about this app.

reviews.title: ⭐ 1 Star — Misleading Free Trial & Terrible Billing Experience
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with this app and its misleading subscription practices. On October 19, I was offered a 7-day FREE trial, followed by a $39.99 annual subscription. I accepted the offer, only to be immediately billed $42.59 instead of receiving the advertised trial.

I canceled the subscription and contacted Apple Support, only to be told that I must pay the $42.59 before I can even request a refund, which isn’t guaranteed.

Now my Apple account is restricted, preventing me from downloading apps or renewing my iCloud storage. My iCloud email is no longer receiving important work-related communications because of this situation.

To make matters worse, the app continues to advertise additional free-trial offers, including 14 days free, despite my previous trial not being honored.

This is completely unacceptable. Customers should not be offered a free trial and then immediately billed for an annual subscription. I would strongly caution others against accepting this app’s promotional offers until these billing issues are addressed.

I just don’t understand how they can just charge you for a subscription that you never ordered. 8 dollars a week? The one time I did try this app a couple years ago, I had very limited success with it accurately differentiating between different plants and types of trees in my yard, so it was of no value to me in my quest to identify all of my plants and learn as much about them as possible, so I could provide the best possible care within my ability and knowledge to do so. I am just very frustrated above everything else that I can be charged so many times, when at the very least, I never intentionally subscribed to the app, and I was denied a refund when requested, and at worst questionable business practices by the App Store and/or this app. I’m not entirely who is doing what because they intentionally don’t allow you to talk to a human or offer any explanation. reviews.title: Did what I wanted but...
reviews.text: I don't normally write reviews but this app has made me do it. I wanted to take a picture to identity a flower which it did, so in that regard the app does a good job, but I was blown away at how LONG it took to just take one single photo. There is, no joke, about 2 minutes of unskippable animation that tells you what this app does and how great it is at doing it. I KNOW WHAT THE APP DOES, I ALREADY DOWNLOADED IT! Why force me through so many pointless cutscenes with no option to skip them? I can't hate on the actual function of the app because it did its job well but the amount of cutscenes that play when you start the app for the first time was absolutely ridiculous and annoyed me enough to give it one star. Like, at least give the option to skip them.

reviews.title: ChatGPT identify plants
reviews.text: 7 yrs ago this app would of been amazing, but chatgpt can identify plants etc and is better than this app as I could ask ChatGPT what do I look for to determine if it is a yucca gigante or another yucca, or one flax or perennial grass (I live in New Zealand). I do love the feel of this app - green button but ui is very noisy as I am not interested in all other stuff — just my garden. The my garden database it allows you to build is not user friendly and NO amazing AI automation tools with my plants eg show me sequential planting of asset1.,2,3 from my garden, show me that planting in autumn v summer. Such a shame as I truelly wanted a my garden app. There is NO encouragement of ecological thinking  — plant native eg show me natives that are like plant xyz, show me natives in this area - intelligent image assessment of a picture or a persons garden. Native is more important than ‘weed’

reviews.title: Inaccurate, doesn’t show any sources, doesn’t save work
reviews.text: I’m really surprised this app has this many high ratings. First of all this app is trying to  charge money tell me that every single one of my plants has a transmittable fungal infection when going and doing other research about the subject suggests this is completely wrong. OK fine someone’s right and I don’t know who it is. But then it doesn’t allow me to save those searches so that I can reference the information and do my own research. I continually have to retake pictures of the plants and ask the same questions. When diagnosing my plant with this mysterious disease called “brown spots” or something nonsensical it doesn’t have any clickable information to read more about this condition. You have to exit and dig down in the plants common problems to find anything remotely similar but usually won’t find anything Word for Word that connects to what your plant was diagnosed with. Frankly this indicates to me that this is all AI nonsense. Furthermore experimenting with the app on the same plant supports this theory because I get a different version of words and slightly different diagnosis with each new iteration. Then I get a canned series of recommendations. Completely untrustworthy. Bunch of bologna with a pretty app.

reviews.title: Frustrating that it’s can’t use verified plant identification in photo at a botanical Gardens to id
reviews.text:
I’ve just been to Sir Harold Hillers

The application picture this should simply allow the identification label when visiting Garden estates to be used to allow a user to update the plant identification based on the photos that they took. 

 This data then could be used to help the database mining system for ‘picture this’ to correctly identify plants moving forward for the wider community if those photos by the user were allowed to be anonymously shared on its system and also because it’s come from a established Estate such as RHS Wisley and so forth then those bits of information can be used precisely and with multiple people taking that same photo in the same Garden estates with the same label would add weight to the original photo
